correctness.rationale: For P not dividing a the two divisible residue classes modulo P are disjoint; each has one excluded residue modulo P² and the remaining residues in those classes have negative sign. For v_P(a)=1 the divisible class overlaps and two residues are excluded; for v_P(a)≥2 only one is excluded. This gives all displayed factors and the two-linear-prime sign test. Monic degree-N residues are uniform at N=D_M as well as above it. The discarded large-square events only replace a bounded signed summand by zero, giving the claimed union bound, with no factor-of-two loss beyond counting both shifts. Grouping the prime-product logarithm by total degree gives H_M, with tail O(2^(−M/2)/M); the normalized Euler factors have summable deviations with exponentially small tails and no zeros. Thus the algebraic relative terms are those of exp(−4H_M), including −2 and 1/3+2=7/3. The verification script was inspected, not executed; the proof is analytical, not inferred from its degree-eleven checks.
